I've just been looking into this as well and it seems like we're coming to the same conclusion: 
- An additional `noise_site` field in the `SimulatorOptions` with values `"L"`, `"M"`, `"R"`, `"before"`, `"after"`
- This allows exact specification of the barrier, and `"before"`/`"after"` are convenience options where the specific barrier is chosen based on the context of the box. Before/after here explicitly means a user wants the error to be applied immediately before or after the ideal gate operation in the simulation.

For the before/after auto-choosing, Claude gave me this rule based on how the box is dressed:
```
_SITE_TO_POSITION = {
    (InjectionSite.BEFORE, DressingMode.LEFT): "M",
    (InjectionSite.AFTER, DressingMode.LEFT): "R",
    (InjectionSite.BEFORE, DressingMode.RIGHT): "L",
    (InjectionSite.AFTER, DressingMode.RIGHT): "M",
}
```
It should be verified but I think this is roughly correct.

This string could be added as a third entry in the tuple of `layer_noise_model`, though it will need to be decided what to do with in the `estimator_options_to_executor_options` conversion function.

There are a couple of further issues here:
- Should this specification be kept optional with a default?
- Special case 1: prep noise
   - There is not always a box associated with preparation, and in this case there is no way to assign a model to it. One option is to add another option to `SimulatorOptions` to specify a noise map that happens *before anything else in the circuit*. It is absolutely critical that it happens before anything else happens, so that it is truly appearing immediately after the preparation operation.
   - If there *is* a box associated with it, the body is empty, and I believe it is constrained to be a left-dressed. This is problematic for the above `_SITE_TO_POSITION` choices: in this case the actual operation we want to model occurs before the box, and if we use the above rules the noise map will be inserted AFTER the dressing, which is not what we want. Here, what we really want, is to assign the noise map to the `"L"` barrier.
- Special case 2: a box with only single qubit gates
   - This is again problematic, e.g. if the box is left dressed, having the noise occur after the dressing but `"before"` the layer is impossible, as the single qubit gates get absorbed into the dressing.

For the special cases: we definitely need an option for inserting a noise map at the very beginning of the circuit regardless. For the empty-box case in the prep-noise situation, what we really want is to assign it to the `"L"` barrier, so this could be handled by raising an error if the user specifies `"before"`/`"after"` in this scenario, and tell them to assign it to an explicit barrier. For the single-qubit only case I'm not sure what to do.

Reviving this issue and marking it is a good first issue, tweaking a bit the scope.

By the time [a job is instantiated](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/0.49.0/qiskit_ibm_runtime/qiskit_runtime_service.py#L1309-L1320) by `service.job()` and `service.jobs()`, we nowadays to have [the information about its status](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/api/qiskit-runtime-rest/tags/jobs#tags__jobs__operations__list_jobs) available.

It should be possible to feed that information at that point in time, to prevent the jobs always being instantiated in the Python side with [an "initialized"](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/0.49.0/qiskit_ibm_runtime/runtime_job_v2.py#L112) state - that causes `job.status()` to always make a query the first time it is invoked. Nowadays it should be less than 5 seconds for it to return, but still, it seems like a call that we can avoid.

There are some unknowns:
* for jobs not in a final state, `job.status()` will still make a HTTP call (and rightfully so, as the semantics of the call is retrieving their current status)
* there is some complexity in how state is handled internally (the `_status` variable and the error message handling), and some complexity due to inheritance
* ideally it would be nice to avoid modifying the `RuntimeJobV2` interface (constructor, adding public methods) _and_ to avoid calling private methods. If having to chose among the two, calling private methods can be more reasonable.  
* edge cases might be present (specifically, the `service.job()` and `service.jobs()` method need to be guaranteed to keep working fully)

## Acceptance criteria

`job.status()` does not need to make a HTTP call when it is in a final state when retrieved via `service.job()` and `service.jobs()`.

> Since [Jordan Borean (@jborean93)](https://github.com/jborean93) maintains sspilib and pyspnego, I am mentioning him here
in case he can clarify whether Authenticode-signed Windows wheels could be
provided for sspilib.

It's not something I would do personally to include in the main PyPI package but technically you could you could vendor or bundle your own copy of `sspilib` and sign the `.pyd` files yourself as part of any distribution you do.

In saying that if you are running on a host that has enabled WDAC/App Control or AppLocker you probably don't want to have Python loaded at all. It needs you to allow `python.exe` and it's runtime dlls to run  and trusted but this means you now have a way to execute arbitrary code and bypass the restrictions of WDAC and co. Python just isn't compatible in this world as it hasn't taken the steps like PowerShell to become an [enlightened applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/design/script-enforcement#script-enforcement-overview) so itself can validate what Python code it can execute safely.

This is related to #3206 and follow-ups - and arguably partly by design.

During these, we settled on "we consider that we use `qiskit_ibm_runtime.QuantumProgram` in all places", and all methods are typed accordingly and make that assumption (ie. the instances [will always have](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/0.50.0/qiskit_ibm_runtime/quantum_program/quantum_program.py#L81) `_semantic_role`). 

I do agree it would be desirable to be able to run `samplomatic.QuantumProgram` - we could:
* add the ability of building `qiskit_ibm_runtime.QuantumProgram` from a `samplomatic.QuantumProgram`
* with that, either consider it is the user's responsibility to convert, or refine the requirement (which can actually be "executor.run() should accept both inputs")

Keeping the rationale of assuming that we use `qiskit_ibm_runtime.QuantumProgram` allows the package to be consistent and prevents edge cases: so I'm aiming to containing the conversion either to user-land or to very specific and targeted user-facing entry points.

Hi Jordan,  
Thanks for your explanation. After investigating further, you were right about this.  
It turned out that Windows Smart App Control was enabled on my machine. I initially encountered the issue with sspilib, but later I got exactly the same kind of error when Qiskit tried to import scipy.linalg: Windows blocked SciPy's _flapack native module because of the application control policy.
This made it clear that the issue was not specific to sspilib, but more generally related to running Python and its native dependencies under such a restrictive application-control policy.
After disabling Smart App Control, both sspilib and scipy.linalg worked normally, without any changes to the packages.
So I agree that signing the sspilib .pyd files in the main PyPI package would not really solve the broader problem. A Python application may depend on many other native .pyd and .dll files from NumPy, SciPy, PySide, etc., and those can be subject to the same restrictions.
Thanks again for pointing me in the right direction and for the explanation about Python not being an enlightened application for App Control.

> E.g. do we need to recommend one way or the other in docs?

I don't think we should recommend one over the other. I believe it should be transparent to the user.

I think keeping the documentation in this package mainly geared towards `qiskit_ibm_runtime.QuantumProgram` still makes sense. It is mostly internal, and the `QuantumProgram`s that get created are also mostly internal (the only user-facing place currently is for the inputs of an `executor` job - which would be a `qiskit_ibm_runtime.QuantumProgram` even if the user submitted a `samplomatic.QuantumProgram`, as it would be converted under the hood once the related PR lands).

For docs that involve `executor.run()` specifically, I don't have a strong opinion. Gearing users towards `samplomatic.QuantumProgram` might sit better with the overall concept of `QuantumProgram` living in `samplomatic` and being more generic. At the same time, we should also be covered by type hints post-this-PR: so I think that part is genuinely a question for product 😄
